title: From a photo to a resin figurine

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Here's a trick. Take a photo, and a few steps later you're holding a little vinyl-style figure of it, printed in resin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay, that sounds like it should be harder than it is. How does it actually work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine wrote it up as a four-step pipeline. First, a reference photo, a clear side or front view. Second, turn it into a chibi vinyl toy image. Third, an image-to-3D model builds the mesh. Fourth, you print.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the AI does two jobs. It restyles the picture, then it builds the 3D shape.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. For the toy image he uses ChatGPT, Midjourney, or ComfyUI with a model called OmniGen2. The prompt is simple: a vinyl chibi figurine, smooth plastic, white background, one character, in a pose that can stand on a base.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hunyuan3D version 2. In his ComfyUI workflow, one graph does both stages. The first stage makes the chibi picture, the second outputs two mesh files at slightly different thresholds. And if your graphics card only has eight to twelve gigabytes of memory, he says to lower a couple of resolution settings.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does it matter much which 3D tool you pick?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Less than you'd think. The page says the clarity of the toy image matters more than the brand of the generator. Mesh tools amplify a bad silhouette, so a blurry start gives you a mushy figure.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Resin, for small parts. Tilt overhangs toward the plate, keep supports light on things like hair and capes, and check for floating islands in the slicer or in UVtools. Skip that check and a failed print can waste hours.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the takeaway is: spend your effort on the 2D image.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Get the picture right, and the rest of the pipeline mostly follows. The full write-up has the diagram, the prompts, the workflow file and the slide deck.
